project.title: Love Saves The Day 2025
project.medium: festival campaign identity and visual toolkit
project.format: Cross-channel campaign spanning lineup reveal, social, print, stage screens, signage, and onsite branding

why: A strong campaign reference because one festival image world is treated as a deployable toolkit: the lineup poster sets the visual tone, while photography, stickers, textures, templates, and motion carry the same energy into feeds, screens, and physical space.

artDirection.title: Type as a living sticker layer
artDirection.study: The case study describes a sticker set that evolved into a typographic playground, giving the campaign a raw, playful layer that can move between static and animated applications.
artDirection.reuse: Build a small vocabulary of type-led stickers that can be rearranged, cropped, and animated without losing recognition.

artDirection.title: People and place as the campaign signal
artDirection.study: Crowd, city, and festival photography replace generic stock imagery and make the local community the campaign's proof of energy.
artDirection.reuse: Use real participants and recognizable places as a recurring image layer when belonging matters more than polish.

artDirection.title: One anchor image across the rollout
artDirection.study: An ultra-close crop of the Brouhaha stage anchors the lineup reveal and establishes a bold, textural tone for print, stories, lanyards, and related assets.
artDirection.reuse: Choose one high-recognition crop as the campaign's rally point, then let every format reinterpret its texture instead of inventing a new hero each time.

artDirection.title: Toolkit without visual drift
artDirection.study: Layered textures and modular templates were made easy for the internal team to deploy while retaining the festival's DIY energy.
artDirection.reuse: Design the handoff as a constrained kit: a few color, texture, type, and crop rules that preserve attitude when others produce the next asset.

channels.study: The lineup artwork is described as moving from print into the wider campaign system.
channels.reuse: Keep the first static key visual legible at poster distance and crop-safe for smaller physical touchpoints.

channels.study: The visual system supports lineup drops, hype-building teasers, artist cards, and stage information in fast-scrolling feeds.
channels.reuse: Separate identity layers from content layers so operational information can change without rebuilding the campaign world.

channels.study: The same visual narrative extends from digital release moments into onsite signage and festival spaces.
channels.reuse: Treat environmental graphics as a continuation of the feed system, with scale and distance as explicit constraints.

motionCutdowns.title: Small motion, high repeatability
motionCutdowns.study: Animated stickers add movement to the campaign's typographic layer and can be reused across social content.
motionCutdowns.reuse: Prefer short, loopable sticker motions with a still-frame fallback for exports, accessibility, and reduced-motion contexts.

motionCutdowns.title: Escalate the same grammar on stage
motionCutdowns.study: The toolkit was designed to flex from frantic feed scrolls to full-stage screen takeovers, keeping the system recognizable at large scale.
motionCutdowns.reuse: Reserve one or two high-contrast transformations for large screens rather than adding unrelated effects.

assets.notes: The source identifies crowd, city, and festival photography as a central direction; no source photography is copied into this library.
assets.reuse: Commission or capture original images with a consistent crop and contrast treatment.

assets.notes: The source's sticker language is proprietary and is not reproduced in the local preview.
assets.reuse: Create original type-led marks with a limited set of transformations and an explicit still fallback.

assets.notes: The case study describes layered textures and modular templates as internal campaign assets; no source files are included.
assets.reuse: Build textures from original CSS, SVG, or licensed material so the system remains portable and rights-safe.

implementation.format: Responsive campaign reference with a hero key visual and reusable static/motion toolkit
implementation.notes: The official Hey! What? case study provides direct evidence for the 2025 campaign scope, art direction, channel rollout, and motion behavior. Implementation details are limited to observed principles; proprietary artwork, fonts, video, and brand assets remain external.

capture.attribution: Hey! What? for Team Love / Love Saves The Day; source photography and campaign assets remain with their respective creators.
